question.text: Which one of the following statement is not true?

options.text: Lactose contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi><mo>-</mo></math>glycosidic linkage between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> of galactose and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> of glucose
Lactose is a reducing sugar and it gives Fehling's test.

Lactose <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>11</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>22</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> is a disaccharide and it contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn></math> hydroxyl groups.

On acid hydrolysis, lactose gives one molecule of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mfenced><mo>+</mo></mfenced><mo>-</mo></math>glucose and one molecule of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mfenced><mo>+</mo></mfenced><mo>-</mo></math>galactose.

solution.text:
The linkage is between C-1 of Galactose and C-4 of Glucose

Lactose (Milk sugar) →H3O⊕β-galactose + β-glucose

C12H22O11

it is hydrolysed by dilute acids or by the enzyme lactase, to an equimolecular mixture of D+-glucose and D+-galactose. Lactose is a reducing sugar.
